title: Planes of symmetry of a regular-polygon-based pyramid
source: Theory IGCSE-19.2 Quick check 1; a regular n-gon based pyramid with congruent triangular faces has n planes of symmetry
stem: How many planes of symmetry does a pyramid have if its base is a regular {n|int}-sided polygon and the triangular faces are congruent?

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: Each plane contains the apex and a line of symmetry of the base, so there are \({A|int}\) planes.
steps.note: A regular n-gon based pyramid with congruent triangular faces has n planes of symmetry.

contexts.note: Includes the original square-based pyramid, 4 planes

title: Planes of symmetry that contain the axis of a regular-polygon prism
source: Theory IGCSE-19.2 Quick check 2; a right prism with a regular n-gon cross-section has n planes containing the axis
stem: How many planes of symmetry of a right prism with a regular {n|int}-sided cross-section contain the axis of the prism?

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: There is one such plane for each line of symmetry of the cross-section, so there are \({A|int}\) planes.
steps.note: Planes containing the axis match the lines of symmetry of the regular n-gon.

contexts.note: Includes the original equilateral triangular prism, 3 axial planes

title: Planes of symmetry of a regular polygonal prism
source: Theory IGCSE-19.2 Quick check 3; an n-gonal prism has n+1 planes
stem: A right prism has a regular \({n|int}\)-sided cross-section and is not a cube. How many planes of symmetry does it have?

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: There are \({n|int}\) planes containing the axis and one plane parallel to the ends, so the total is \({A|int}\).
steps.note: n planes through the axis plus the mid-plane.

contexts.note: Includes the original regular pentagonal prism
